Testing objectives and considerations
- Primary lifts: Back Squat, Deadlift (conventional or preferred technique), and Bench Press.
- Secondary lift for context (optional): Overhead Press or a pulling variation (e.g., Bent-over Row) if you want a broader strength snapshot.
- Safety: Use a progressive warm-up with submaximal attempts; avoid attempting all maximal lifts in a single day if fatigue risks injury.
- Scheduling: Plan testing on a dedicated day or split across two days to maintain performance and safety.
- Equipment: Ensure access to a reliable lifting platform/barbell, calibrated weights, and spotter/barbell holder as needed.

Preparation timeline (Phase 3, weeks 9–12)
- Week 9–10: Begin tapering volume on main lifts to freshen before 1RM attempts. Maintain technique and speed work, reduce accessory volume by ~20–30%.
- Week 11: Light to moderate loading with performance-focused sets, including a single planned 1RM attempt per lift on separate sessions or consecutive days with adequate rest.
- Week 12: Optional retest or alternative top single reps if needed; this week can serve as a deload/transition if you’re not feeling fully recovered.

Suggested testing protocol (two options)

Option A: Single-day triple-testing with rest
- Day plan: Test Squat, Bench, and Deadlift in this order with ample rest between attempts (15–20 minutes for main lifts, longer if needed).
- Warm-up progression (example for each lift):
  - 5–10 minutes general warm-up (light cardio + mobility)
  - Specific warm-ups: 5 sets building to the opening attempt
  - Example progression for squat:
    - Bar x 5 (20 kg)
    - 40% 1RM x 5
    - 60% x 3
    - 70% x 2
    - 80% x 1
    - 90% x 1
    - 95% x 1 (or 1–2 reps if technical and safe)
    - Attempt 1RM: chosen weight
  - Repeat a similar ramp for bench and deadlift, adjusting weights.
- Attempt structure:
  - Squat: 1 attempt at target; if fails, back off to a conservative second attempt (e.g., 2.5–5% below first failed attempt) if technique remains solid, else stop.
  - Bench: same structure; ensure a reliable spot and arch/foot position.
  - Deadlift: given higher CNS demand, consider giving more rest between attempts (3–5 minutes).
- Rest and safety:
  - 3–5 minutes between heavy attempts for squat/deadlift; 2–4 minutes for bench.
  - Have a trained spotter and safety bars; use belt, wrist wraps, knee sleeves as needed.

Option B: Split-day testing (recommended if fatigue is a concern)
- Day 1: Squat + Bench
  - Warm-up and attempt progression as above
  - Target 1RM day 1: Squat; day 2: Bench
- Day 2: Deadlift
  - Warm-up and attempt progression as above
- Rationale: Reduces CNS fatigue and technique breakdown risk by separating lifts.

Load progression guidelines
- If client has clean technique and previous progressive loads, plan modest jumps:
  - Squat/Deadlift/Bench: 2.5–5% increases per successful attempt.
  - If attempting a PB (personal best) and missing, consider a smaller increment (2.5%) for a second attempt within the same lift.
- If any lift shows form breakdown or pain, revert to a safer max by adjusting the final attempt downward.

Safety and readiness checks
- Use recent training data to estimate initial 1RM or 5RM as a baseline; if you lack recent maxes, use a conservative approach using RPE targets to estimate 1RM.
- Ensure you’re fueling well in the days leading up to testing; prioritize protein and carbohydrates around test days.
- Hydration, sleep, and stress management are important; avoid deloading too close to the test.

Documentation and data tracking
- Record all attempted weights, reps completed, and RPE for each lift.
- Note any technical cues that helped or hindered performance (bar path, bracing, foot stance).
- Compare end-of-phase 3 numbers to baseline estimates (if available) and to the in-program progression targets.
- Optional: capture video of lifts for technique review and future programming adjustments.

Sample schedule recommendations
- Week 9–10: Reduce volume on main lifts by 20–30% while keeping intensity near 85–95% for the last sets; practice ramp-ups and technique.
- Week 11: 1RM attempt day(s). Keep a Week 11 plan with 1RM attempts for squat, bench, and deadlift across two sessions or a single day if fatigue permits.
- Week 12: Optional retest or maintain light work; use this week as a full rest or active recovery focusing on mobility and technique review.

Adaptive alternatives
- If any lift is restricted due to injury or ongoing niggles, substitute a safe alternative for measurement (e.g., leg press 1RM estimate, bench press 1RM with incline or floor press as a proxy).
- If testing feels unsafe on a given day, reschedule within Week 11 or Week 12 windows and avoid forcing a max attempt.

Below is a consolidated, fully integrated 12-week strength + hypertrophy program with all prior adjustments rolled in. It includes: weekly structure, phase goals, detailed lifting plans (weeks 1–12 with specific exercises, sets, reps, and RPE targets), the integrated cardio plan (2–3 days/week), the HIIT day (one per week, optional), the plyometric/power day (one per week), the added 1RM testing plan at the end of Phase 3, and the nutrition framework previously provided. The schedule assumes a 4-day lifting week (Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri) with optional cardio/HIIT on other days and a dedicated plyometric/power day slotted within the lifting cycle. Phase boundaries and progression are explicit.

Starting context
- Client: 26-year-old female recreational lifter, on combined oral contraceptive pill (no cycle-based adjustments required). Cleared for full intensity.
- Training goal: 12-week strength + hypertrophy with progressive overload, balanced accessory work, and added cardio/HIIT and plyometric/power components.
- Start: 2026-06-01 (Week 1).

Weekly structure overview
- Lifting days: 4 days per week
  - Day A: Squat emphasis + push
  - Day B: Pull emphasis
  - Day C: Upper push hypertrophy
  - Day D: Lower body velocity/accessory (and an integrated plyometric/power focus)
- Cardio: 2–3 sessions per week (Phase 1: build foundation; Phase 2: build work capacity with minimal interference; Phase 3: maintain with recovery emphasis)
- HIIT day: 1 per week (Phase 2; optional or alternate, placed to minimize lifting interference)
- Plyometric/Power day: 1 per week (integrated within or adjacent to the lifting schedule; details below)
- 1RM testing: Phase 3 end (Weeks 9–12), with a structured progression and two options (single day or split across two days)

Phase structure and goals
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and hypertrophy build
  - Emphasis: moderate volume, progressive overload with hypertrophy focus, robust technique
  - Reps: main lifts 6–8; accessory 8–12; core work included
  - RPE: main lifts around 8; volume work 7–8
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength emphasis with maintained hypertrophy
  - Emphasis: higher loading on main lifts; 4–5 sets of main lifts; lower reps with higher intensity (RPE 8–9)
  - Accessory work maintains 8–12 reps; volume adjusted to support recovery
  - Cardio: HIIT integrated (optional/based on recovery)
  - Plyometric/Power: 1 day integrated weekly
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Peak strength and consolidation; test window
  - Emphasis: peak lifts, maintain hypertrophy via accessories, controlled volume, 1RM testing in Week 11–12
  - Cardio: maintenance with reduced volume if fatigue; HIIT optional
  - Plyometrics: maintain but monitor fatigue
  - 1RM testing planned for end of Phase 3

Detailed plan by week (weeks 1–12)

Phase 1: Foundation + Hypertrophy (Weeks 1–4)
Weekly template (repeat with progressive loading; Week 1 is baseline dial-in)

Week 1
- Day A (Squat emphasis + push)
  - Back Squat: 4x6–8 (RPE 8)
  - Front Squat or Goblet Squat: 3x8–10
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x8–10
  - Walking Lunges or Step-Ups: 3x10 per leg
  - Push Press or Overhead Press: 3–4x6–8
  - Bench Variation (DB or Barbell): 3x8–10
  - Core: Plank 3x45s
- Day B (Pull emphasis)
  - Deadlift (snappier 4x4–6 or 3x4–6 if technique needed)
  - Pull-ups/Lat Pulldown: 3–4x6–10
  - Barbell/Dumbbell Row: 3–4x8–10
  - Hip Bridge or Hip Thrust: 3x10–12
  - Hamstring Curl: 3x10–12
  - Bicep Curl: 2–3x10–12
  - Core: Hanging Leg Raises 3x12–15
- Day C (Upper push)
  - Incline DB/BB Press: 3–4x8–10
  - Seated/Standing DB Press: 3x8–10
  - Dumbbell Lateral Raises: 3x12–15
  - Cable Face Pulls: 3x12–15
  - Chest Fly (DB or Cable): 3x10–12
  - Triceps Pushdown / Skull Crushers: 3x10–12
  - Core: Optional 3x12–15
- Day D (Lower body hypertrophy)
  - Leg Press or Front Squat: 3–4x10–12
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x10–12 per leg
  - Glute Ham Raise / Nordic (assisted if needed): 3x6–8
  - Calf Raises: 4x12–15
  - Core Circuit: 3 rounds (45s plank, 30s side planks each side, 12 per side bird-dog)

Phase 1 notes
- Week 1–2: Dial in technique; start with conservative loads.
- Week 3–4: Slightly increase volume or load on main lifts if recovery allows.

Phase 2: Strength Focus (Weeks 5–8)
New adjustments to emphasize higher intensity on main lifts (2-5% increases weekly where possible), maintain hypertrophy via accessories.

Week 5 (Anchor)
- Day A – Squat emphasis
  - Back Squat: 5x4–5 (RPE 8–9)
  - Pause Squat or Tempo Squat: 3x3–5 (RPE 8)
  - Front Squat or Light Bulgarian: 3x5–6 (RPE 8)
  - Bench/Incline Press: 3–4x6–8 (RPE 8)
  - Overhead Press: 3–4x6–8 (RPE 8)
  - Accessory chest/shoulder: 2–3x8–12
  - Core: Pallof press 3x10 ea side
- Day B – Pull emphasis
  - Deadlift: 4–5x4–6 (RPE 8–9)
  - Barbell Row: 3–4x6–8
  - Weighted Pull-ups/Lat Pulldown: 3–4x6–8
  - T-bar/Single-arm Row: 3x8–10
  - Hamstring accessory: 3x8–10
  - Core: Carries 2x30–60s
- Day C – Upper push hypertrophy
  - Bench Press: 4–5x5–7 (RPE 8–9)
  - Overhead Press: 3–4x6–8
  - Dips/Push-ups: 3x8–12
  - Chest-supported Row / Cable Row: 3x10–12
  - Lateral Raises + Face Pulls: 3x12–15
  - Triceps accessory: 3x10–12
- Day D – Lower body velocity/accessory
  - Speed Squats or Light Front Squats: 3x3–5 (velocity focus, 40–60% 1RM)
  - Hip Thrust: 3–4x6–8
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x6–8 per leg
  - Calf Raises: 4x12–15
  - Core: Plank variations 3x45–60s

Week 6
- Repeat Week 5 with small incremental load increases on main lifts (2.5–5% where technique holds); keep accessories at 8–12 reps.

Week 7
- Maintain volume, push main lifts 3–4x4–6 on primary movements; add slight progression on accessory lifts for hypertrophy.

Week 8
- Optional deload or light progression: If feeling fatigued, reduce total volume by 10–20% on accessory work and maintain main lift intensities; else continue progression.

Phase 3: Peak & Consolidation (Weeks 9–12)
Focus on peaking lifts, controlled volume, and starting to plan 1RM testing in Week 11–12. Carbs maintained to support heavy lifting and recovery.

Week 9
- Maintain Phase 2 intensity but begin to drop some volume to allow recovery.
- Day A: Back Squat 4x3–5 (RPE 9)
- Day B: Deadlift 3–4x2–4 (RPE 9)
- Day C: Bench 4x3–5 (RPE 9)
- Day D: Lower body velocity/acc 3x3–5 (velocity emphasis)

- HIIT: Optional 1 session if recovered

Week 10
- Similar to Week 9 with slight reductions in total reps; ensure technique remains sharp.

Week 11
- 1RM Testing window (if chosen)
  - Plan to test 1RM on Squat, Bench, and Deadlift with 1–2 days between lifts (Option A: single day with ramped attempts; Option B: split across two days to reduce CNS fatigue)
  - Warm-ups: progressive ladder culminating in 1RM attempts
  - Attempt strategy: start with a safe opening attempt, escalate by 2.5–5% increments; if fail, make a safe second attempt within reasonable range
- If not testing, maintain lifting with lightened volume and practice technique and speed work.

Week 12
- Optional retest or deload/active recovery
- If testing occurred in Week 11, Week 12 can be an active recovery week with mobility, light cardio, and technique work. If not tested, keep a light week with mobility focus and technique.

1RM testing protocol (end Phase 3)
- Primary lifts tested: Back Squat, Bench Press, Deadlift
- Warm-up ladder per lift: light reps up to 90–95% attempt range
- Rest: 3–5 minutes between heavy attempts
- Safety: Spotters in place; bar path and bracing checked; if technique fails, abort attempt and take a safer approach
- Data capture: record actual weight, reps, RPE, and video for technique review
- Optional secondary lift: Overhead Press or Bent-over Row for a broader strength snapshot

Nutritional framework (recap and integration with Phase changes)
- Protein target: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day (adjust based on body weight)
- Calorie target: maintenance to small surplus in Phase 1 (0–250 kcal/day), modest surplus in Phase 2 (150–350 kcal/day), adjust in Phase 3 as needed with progress
- Carbohydrates: higher around training days; lower on rest days
- Fats: 0.6–1.0 g/kg/day; 20–30% of total calories as a starting point
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day; adjust for climate and activity
- Supplements: Creatine 3–5 g daily; consider Vitamin D if needed; Omega-3s 1–2 g/day; caffeine 3–6 mg/kg pre-workout as tolerated
- Peri-workout nutrition: protein + carb around workouts (20–40 g protein + 30–60 g carbs pre-workout; 20–40 g protein + 40–60 g carbs post-workout)

Cardio and HIIT integration (recap)
- Cardio: 2–3 sessions/week; phases as above
- HIIT day: 1 per week during Phase 2; optional or reduced in Phase 3 if fatigue
- Modality choices: cycling, rowing, incline treadmill walk, or bodyweight options
- Scheduling: away from the heaviest lifting days or after lighter sessions if necessary

Plyometric / Power day (recap)
- 1 plyometric/power day per week
- Phase 1: technique and safe landings
- Phase 2: incremental intensity
- Phase 3: maintain quality with possible substitutions to velocity-based or light Olympic-lift variants

Safety and progression guardrails
- Always prioritize form on main lifts; reduce volume or intensity if form breaks
- Use warm-ups and mobility; ensure joints and tendons are getting adequate recovery
- Use autoregulation (RPE-based progression) if weekly progress stalls
- Ensure at least one full rest or active recovery day per week
- If any pain or overtraining signs appear, scale back HIIT, plyometrics, and/or cardio

What’s included in this consolidated plan
- Weeks 1–4: Phase 1 hypertrophy foundation with 4 lifting days
- Weeks 5–8: Phase 2 strength emphasis; 4 lifting days plus optional HIIT and integrated plyometric/power day
- Weeks 9–12: Phase 3 peak strength; 4 lifting days, optional HIIT, and plyometric/power day; Week 11–12 reserved for 1RM testing end-of-phase
- Nutrition: protein-focused, phase-aligned calorie targets, peri-workout nutrition, micronutrients, supplementation guidance
- Cardio: 2–3 sessions/week, including lower-impact HIIT option
- Plyometric/Power: 1 dedicated day per week
- 1RM testing plan: structured end-of-phase testing with safety protocols

Notes and customization
- If you share precise body weight, height, current 1RM estimates (if available) or 5RM/3RM for the squat, bench, and deadlift, I can convert this into exact week-by-week loading tables with precise loads, RPE targets, and run-level progression (e.g., 5-week microcycles with exact weights per set).
- If equipment availability or client preferences differ (e.g., limited access to a platform, no squat rack, or no high boxes for plyometrics), I’ll tailor the exercises and progression accordingly.
